title: Lecture 1 — digital abstraction and number systems
summary: Digital systems replace continuous physical values with discrete logic states. Bits, voltage ranges, positional notation, and binary conversion provide the language for representing numbers in hardware.
body: Digital design assigns symbolic states to ranges of physical voltages. Those states become bits, and positional notation gives each bit a power-of-two weight. Weighted sums convert binary to decimal; repeated division converts decimal integers to binary. Bit width then determines how many distinct unsigned values a register can store.
